item.text: [{"taxonId":124357,"summary":"A large genus of perennial spring flowers in the lily family, Gagea is found mainly in Eurasia, with a few species extending into North Africa and one into North America. Many appear briefly in early spring and retreat to underground bulbs by mid-spring or summer.","humanEdibility":"unknown","edibilityNote":null,"evidence":{"summary":["s1:p2","s1:p5","s1:p9"],"humanEdibility":[]}},{"taxonId":124387,"summary":"A genus of mosses, Aulacomnium has a circumpolar distribution.","humanEdibility":"unknown","edibilityNote":null,"evidence":{"summary":["s1:p1"],"humanEdibility":[]}},{"taxonId":124833,"summary":"A genus of about 30 flowering-plant species, Caralluma occurs in tropical Africa, the Arabian Peninsula, India, Sri Lanka and Myanmar. Several taxa in the genus are valued as food.","humanEdibility":"yes","edibilityNote":"Several taxa are valued as food; C. adscendens has bitter, salty succulent branches eaten raw.","evidence":{"summary":["s1:p1","s1:p4"],"humanEdibility":["s1:p2","s1:p4"]}},{"taxonId":124842,"summary":"A flowering-plant genus native to Africa and the Arabian Peninsula, Adenium is valued for colorful flowers and unusual swollen stem bases and is often grown as bonsai.
